q: 1. The purpose of reinforcement in pre stress concrete is
options: to impart initial compressive stress in concrete
explain: In prestressed concrete, the tendons/reinforcement are stressed and anchored specifically to impart an initial compressive stress into the concrete before service loads are applied.

q: 2. The mix proportions of cement mortar to be placed in the joints in precast pre stressed member is
explain: As specified in this text, the cement mortar used for filling joints between precast prestressed members is proportioned at 1:1.5 (cement:sand).

q: 3. The cement concrete in which high compressive stresses are artificially induced before its actual use is called
explain: Prestressed concrete is specifically defined as concrete in which internal compressive stresses are deliberately induced before service loading, to counteract anticipated tensile stresses.

q: 4. The mix used in the grouting of ducts in post tensioned pre-stressed concrete is
options: cement or cement sand mortar grout
explain: For grouting ducts in post-tensioned prestressed concrete, a neat cement grout (without sand) is generally used to ensure it flows and fills the narrow duct completely.

q: 5. The grouting of ducts in post tensioned pre stressed concrete works should be done up to pressure of about (in MPa)
explain: As per the grouting practice referenced in this text, ducts in post-tensioned members are grouted under a pressure of about 0.7 MPa.

q: 6. The approximate loss of pre stress due to creep in steel in pre stressed concrete is about
explain: As per typical prestress loss values referenced in this text, loss due to relaxation/creep of steel is about 3%.

q: 7. The approximate loss of pre stress due to creep in concrete in pre stressed concrete is about
explain: Creep of concrete under sustained prestress causes a loss of about 6% in the initial prestressing force, as per the values used in this text.

q: 8. The approximate loss of pre stress due shrinkage of concrete in pre stressed concrete is about
explain: Shrinkage of concrete leads to a shortening of the member and a corresponding loss of prestress, approximately 3% as per this text.

q: 9. Cube strength of controlled concrete to be used for pretensioned and post-tensioned work respectively should not be less than
explain: For prestressed concrete work, the required minimum cube strengths differ for pretensioned (420 kg/cm²) and post-tensioned (350 kg/cm²) systems due to their different stress transfer mechanisms.

q: 10. The approximate loss of pre stress pre-tensioned concrete beam is about
explain: Total combined losses (elastic shortening, creep, shrinkage, relaxation) in pre-tensioned concrete beams are typically higher, in the range of 20 to 25%.

q: 11. The approximate loss of pre-stress post tensioned concrete beam is about
explain: Total prestress losses in post-tensioned members are generally somewhat lower than in pre-tensioned members, falling in the range of about 15 to 20%.

q: 12. Endurance limit of mild steel is approximately equal to
explain: The endurance (fatigue) limit of mild steel is approximately 0.5 times its ultimate tensile strength, a commonly cited approximation in material science.

q: 13. Normally pre stressing wires are arranged in the
explain: Prestressing tendons/wires are usually placed near the bottom (tension) zone of the beam to counteract the tensile stresses caused by service loads.

q: 14. Most common method of pre stressing used for factory product in is
explain: The long line method, where multiple units are cast and tensioned along a long prestressing bed simultaneously, is the most common technique used in factory precast production.

q: 15. Which of the following losses of pre stress occurs only in pre tensioning and not in post tensioning
explain: In pre-tensioning, the tendons are stressed and anchored before the concrete is cast, so elastic shortening of concrete transfers directly as an additional loss unique to this method, unlike post-tensioning.

q: 16. Pre stress loss due to friction occurs
explain: Friction losses occur due to contact between the tendon and the duct wall/curvature during the stressing operation, which is a feature specific to post-tensioned construction.

q: 17. Which of the following has high tensile strength?
explain: Cold drawn wires undergo strain hardening during the drawing process, giving them significantly higher tensile strength than plain hot rolled wires.

q: 18. High carbon content in steel causes
options: decrease in tensile strength but increase in ductility
increase in tensile strength but decrease in ductility
decrease in tensile strength and ductility
increase in tensile strength and ductility
explain: Higher carbon content in steel increases its hardness and tensile strength but reduces its ductility, making it more brittle.

q: 19. Cube strength of controlled concrete to be used for pre tensioned and post tensioned w respectively should not be less than
explain: As per the specifications referenced in this text, the minimum cube strength required is 42 MPa for pre-tensioned work and 35 MPa for post-tensioned work.

q: 20. Ultimate strength of cold drawn high steel wires
options: increases with increase in diameter of bar
decreases with increase in diameter of bar
doesn't depend on diameter of bar
explain: Due to the reduced degree of cold working achievable in thicker sections, the ultimate tensile strength of cold drawn high-tensile steel wires decreases as the wire diameter increases.

q: 21. Pre-stressing losses in post tensioned and pre tensioned beams are respectively
explain: As per the values used in this text, the overall prestress loss is about 15% for post-tensioned beams and 20% for pre-tensioned beams.

q: 22. The minimum grade of concrete prescribed for prestressed construction is
explain: Prestressed concrete construction requires higher strength concrete to handle prestressing forces, with a minimum grade of M40 prescribed for pre-tensioned systems.

q: 23. The major loss of prestressed concrete is caused due to
explain: Prestress losses in prestressed concrete occur due to a combination of factors: creep of concrete, relaxation of steel tendons, and shrinkage of concrete, all contributing together.

q: 24. Prestress is imparted to concrete by bearing in
explain: In post-tensioning, the prestressing force is transferred to the concrete through end anchorages bearing against the concrete member, unlike pre-tensioning where it is transferred by bond.

q: 25. The mix proportion of cement mortar to be used in the joints in precast prestressed member is
explain: A relatively rich mortar mix of 1:1.5 (cement:sand) is recommended for filling joints between precast prestressed concrete units to ensure adequate strength and durability.

q: 26. The diameter of high tensile steel tendons used is
explain: High tensile steel wires used as tendons in prestressed concrete typically range from about 5 mm to 8 mm in diameter.

q: 27. The minimum clear spacing for single wires used in pre-tension system is
options: 2 times the diameter of the wire and max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
3 times the diameter of the wire and max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
2 times the diameter of the wire and 1.5 times max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
3 times the diameter of the wire and 1.5 times max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
explain: IS code requires the minimum clear spacing between single pre-tensioned wires to be the greater of 3 times the wire diameter or 1.5 times the maximum aggregate size, to ensure proper compaction and bond.

q: 28. The minimum clear spacing of non-grouped cables or large bars shall be
options: maximum size of cable or bar
5 mm plus maximum size of aggregate
explain: The code specifies the minimum clear spacing for non-grouped cables/large bars as whichever is greatest among 40 mm, the cable/bar size, or 5 mm plus the maximum aggregate size.

q: 29. The minimum clear horizontal spacing between groups of cables or ducts of grouped cables shall be greater of
options: 30 mm or 5 mm more than maximum size of aggregate
40 mm or 5 mm more than maximum size of aggregate
30 mm or maximum size of aggregate
40 mm or maximum size of aggregate
explain: The code requires the minimum clear horizontal spacing between groups/ducts of grouped cables to be the greater of 40 mm or 5 mm more than the maximum aggregate size, to permit proper concrete placement.

q: 30. The minimum clear vertical spacing between groups of cables or ducts of grouped cables shall be
explain: For grouped cables/ducts, the code specifies a minimum clear vertical spacing of 50 mm between groups to ensure adequate concrete cover and compaction.

q: 31. The grouting of ducts in post-tensioned prestressed concrete causes
explain: Grouting bonds the tendon to the surrounding concrete, which improves load transfer (reducing deflection and crack width) while also protecting the tendon from corrosion — all benefits occur together.

q: 32. A parabolic tendon in prestressed beam causes an equivalent balancing
explain: A parabolic tendon profile produces a uniformly varying upward transverse force along its length, which acts as an equivalent distributed load balancing the external gravity loads on the beam.

q: 33. An increase in strain in a concrete member at constant stress is called
explain: Creep is defined as the gradual increase in strain in concrete under a sustained constant stress over time.

q: 34. In case of prestressed concrete, prestressing force is
explain: Prestressing induces a compressive force in the concrete section (via tensioned tendons) so that tensile stresses from external loads are counteracted.

q: 35. In case of prestressed concrete
options: load carrying capacity of member increases
quantity of concrete is saved for same grade
quantity of steel is saved for same grade
explain: Prestressing utilizes the full section more efficiently, so it increases load-carrying capacity while also economizing on both concrete and steel quantities compared to ordinary RCC — all these benefits occur.

q: 36. The purpose of reinforcement in prestressed concrete is :
options: to impact initial compressive stress in concrete
explain: The prestressing steel is tensioned specifically to impart an initial compressive stress into the concrete section before service loads are applied, which is the primary purpose in prestressed members.

q: 37. The cold bent test is conducted in a steel bar to determine :
explain: The cold bend test checks the ductility of reinforcement bars by bending a test specimen through a specified angle, typically 90 degrees, without cracking.

q: 38. For the same design load, the weight of concrete in a prestressed concrete as compared to ordinary reinforced concrete is less by :
explain: Because prestressed members use the full section more efficiently by pre-compressing the concrete, they require considerably less concrete — typically about 50% less — than an equivalent ordinary RCC member for the same load.
